thesis: As machine cognition becomes more abundant, the Obelisk should increasingly organize education around durable human scarcities and responsibilities without abandoning deep knowledge.

scarcities.name: Attention
scarcities.why: Human time and conscious attention remain finite while generated information explodes.
scarcities.formation: deep reading; priority; refusal; contemplation; long projects

scarcities.name: Ground truth and trustworthy evidence
scarcities.why: Plausible synthesis becomes cheap; reality and provenance remain costly.
scarcities.formation: measurement; primary sources; replication; fieldwork; source genealogy

scarcities.name: Judgment
scarcities.why: Option generation becomes cheap while selection under competing criteria remains consequential.
scarcities.formation: comparison; decision records; forecasting; ethics; systems thinking

scarcities.name: Taste
scarcities.why: Abundance increases the value of discriminating quality, coherence, originality and appropriateness.
scarcities.formation: exemplars; blind ranking; criticism; making; revision; curation

scarcities.name: Legitimate ends
scarcities.why: Optimization cannot decide which objectives deserve authority.
scarcities.formation: philosophy; politics; rights; public reason; stakeholder reasoning

scarcities.name: Accountability
scarcities.why: Delegation can diffuse responsibility precisely when systems have greater consequence.
scarcities.formation: decision rights; provenance; viva; incident review; recourse

scarcities.name: Trustworthy relationships
scarcities.why: Synthetic interaction can be abundant while mutual obligation, vulnerability and shared history remain human achievements.
scarcities.formation: listening; care; conflict repair; friendship; family; mentorship; community

scarcities.name: Commitment and courage
scarcities.why: Knowing optimal advice does not make a person act, persist, sacrifice or stand responsible under pressure.
scarcities.formation: long projects; service; leadership; physical challenge; public commitments

scarcities.name: Embodied competence
scarcities.why: Bodies, materials, places and tacit skill resist purely linguistic substitution.
scarcities.formation: movement; craft; repair; experiments; fieldwork; emergency readiness

scarcities.name: Meaning and identity
scarcities.why: Automated productivity cannot answer what a life is for or which commitments make it worth living.
scarcities.formation: philosophy; religion/worldviews; literature; art; biography; reflective practice

scarcities.name: Institutional wisdom
scarcities.why: Powerful systems act through organizations, laws, markets and infrastructures that can fail even when individual advice is excellent.
scarcities.formation: Human Worlds; governance labs; organizational design; law; economics; history

scarcities.name: Physical resources and ecological capacity
scarcities.why: Compute and automation remain embedded in energy, materials, land, water, infrastructure and ecosystems.
scarcities.formation: Earth systems; energy; materials; industrial systems; ecology; resilience

scarcities.name: Plural human perspective
scarcities.why: Optimization from one model or culture can erase legitimate difference and minority interests.
scarcities.formation: languages; global history; comparative philosophy; anthropology; arts; constitutional pluralism

scarcities.name: Stewardship across time
scarcities.why: Increasing technological power expands the consequences of decisions for children, institutions and future generations.
scarcities.formation: long-horizon scenarios; irreversible-risk analysis; history; ethics; institution building
